gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-sen: Stencil-cut and loud, Wallpoet sets a heavy tone with its high-rising lowercase. And Sen follows in a single constant line, tall and modern, giving the shouting heading something quiet to lean on.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-sofia-sans: Warnes stretches out with ink strokes that taper before they touch. Sofia Sans follows in a uniform line with tall, rounded letters and a clear opening, so a long page feels steady and easy to move through.
gen-irish-grover-gf-sofia-sans-semi-cond: Sturdy, oversized lowercase makes Irish Grover look friendly and chunky. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed sits beneath it with a constant stencil-like line and wide curve entrances, which keeps the softer heading from crowding the text.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-roboto: Roboto reads with generous mouths on its round letters and lowercase that sits close to capital height. Goldman, wide and commanding above it, supplies the volume while the body stays quiet.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-abeezee: Luckiest Guy has a high mean line and ink that looks poured at one width, loud and cheerful. ABeeZee does the opposite job, with approachable terminals that finish clear of the stem and keep text easy to follow.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-aldrich: Aldrich reads tall and crisp, with round letters that look cupped. Luckiest Guy brings the cheer, and that gap between a loud poured heading and a tight, modern body is what makes the pair work.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-alexandria: Cheerful from the first letter, Luckiest Guy looks poured at one width, with an e that opens right. Alexandria's wide terminals make a tidy partner.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-amiko: Luckiest Guy sets its mean line high and pours its ink at one width, which makes it loud and cheerful. Amiko's outward-pointing terminals tone things down.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-anek-bangla: Every glyph in Luckiest Guy looks drawn with one fat tip, set under a high mean line. Anek Bangla's wide, barely curled s is the strongest foil.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-anek-devanagari: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy shouts without any calligraphic shading to guide the eye. And Anek Devanagari answers with open mouths and a tall middle zone, so longer text moves along comfortably.
